title: Watch debounce state is lost on backend restart
observed_behavior: The current manager keeps baseline, stability tracker, and pending intent only in process memory. A new manager records an already-present candidate as its startup baseline, resets pending_work, and skips the unchanged file on later scans.
expected_invariant: A candidate observed before a backend restart must remain eligible after its stability window or receive a durable, explicit, duplicate-safe disposition.
root_cause: Watch observation and pending-intent authority has process lifetime, while startup rebasing is treated as authoritative discovery state.
failure_scenario: A source arrives shortly before a normal or abnormal backend restart. The new backend baselines that file, it never becomes a stable detection, and automatic ingestion silently misses it.
evidence: Both named current files are byte-identical to baseline a8bf6e1dda9629e6f818ba12f2c8274362923372.
manager.py lines 123-142 initialize only in-memory baseline, tracker, and pending_work state.

manager.py lines 417-444 record a fresh baseline and skip unchanged baseline entries.
Current test names and exact source search found no restart-inside-debounce persistence or reconciliation path.
safeguard_gap: No observation or pending-intent evidence survives or reconciles backend restart.

title: Token rotation can still commit before final join-blob validation
observed_behavior: The facade validates a shorter placeholder blob, commits token changes through _coordinator_join_token, and only then encodes the final blob with the real longer token. A final size failure returns no blob and has no transaction-wide rollback.
expected_invariant: The exact candidate secret and complete transfer blob must be validated before any token authority changes, or every config/app-state/runtime mutation must be compensated atomically on failure.
root_cause: Preflight uses a differently sized surrogate secret and final blob construction occurs outside the token-mutation compensation boundary.
failure_scenario: A near-limit library payload passes placeholder preflight, token rotation invalidates existing worker credentials, final exact-token encoding exceeds the 32-KiB limit, and no replacement blob reaches the operator.
evidence: facade.py, join.py, and auth.py are all byte-identical to the historical baseline.
facade.py lines 241-261 encodes preflight-token-0123456789, calls the mutating token helper, then performs final encoding.
_coordinator_join_token lines 117-191 can save config/app state or update a running coordinator before returning.
join.py lines 92-103 rejects decoded material over NETWORK_JOIN_BLOB_MAX_DECODED_BYTES.
The prior exact near-limit reproduction remains applicable because every responsible current byte is unchanged.
existing_safeguards: targeted rollback when running-token update itself fails
safeguard_gap: Final exact-token encoding failure is after mutation and outside compensation; the placeholder is not size-equivalent to the generated token.
tests_present: network join and token tests cover ordinary success, bounds, confirmations, and some targeted rollback paths
tests_missing: near-limit exact-token failure leaves all authorities unchanged
injected final-encode failure compensates config, app state, and runtime
two-process auth recovery and packaged restart
recommended_remediation: Generate the exact candidate token and encode the complete candidate blob before mutation, then commit config/app-state/runtime under one compensating transaction and return the prevalidated blob only after commit.
remediation_risk: High: token rollback can lock out workers or leak secrets; preserve redaction, avoid journaling secret payloads, and prove all authority layers restore exactly.
validation_rung: Join/settings/runtime transaction tests, Local API secret/journal tests, two-process auth recovery, packaged restart, and strict packet coverage.
prior_audit_relationship: Reconciled independently by exact current-byte identity and line review; the previously reproduced transaction ordering is unchanged.

title: Coordinator join-blob creation still bypasses configured role authority
observed_behavior: The coordinator join-blob command reads configured role only to echo it in response metadata. Standalone or worker configurations can call the route, mutate token authority, and mint coordinator credentials; the WebView gates only on route availability.
expected_invariant: Coordinator secret creation must require coordinator role, or use a separately named and documented offline-bootstrap authority with explicit mutation scope.
root_cause: Local authentication and confirmations are treated as sufficient authorization without a shared configured-role/setup authority contract.
failure_scenario: An authenticated local caller in standalone or worker mode invokes coordinator join-blob creation, rotates/persists token state, and receives credentials for a role the configured backend does not own.
evidence: All three named current paths are byte-identical to the historical baseline.
facade.py line 224 reads role, but lines 241-299 perform creation and only include role in success/error data; no role precondition exists.
The route contract contains confirmations and secret-handling metadata but no coordinator-role guard.
lifecycle.view.js lines 199-219 enables the coordinator create button whenever the route is present.

safeguard_gap: No configured-role authorization or explicit offline-bootstrap authority exists.
tests_present: ordinary coordinator join-blob and strict confirmation tests
tests_missing: standalone and worker reject create/rotate with zero writes
coordinator succeeds
any offline bootstrap path has separate authority, naming, confirmation, and secret-safety tests
recommended_remediation: Require configured coordinator role, or introduce a separately named backend offline-bootstrap command with explicit authority and mutation contract; keep the decision backend-owned and mirror capability in the WebView.
remediation_risk: Medium-high: over-restricting may break intended first-run bootstrap, while an implicit exception preserves the authorization bypass; product policy must be explicit.
validation_rung: Facade and Local API role matrix, WebView route/capability tests, secret/journal checks, packaged setup flow, and strict packet coverage.
